title: La Silla at night
caption: The night sky over La Silla Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at La Silla Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: This photograph shows the night sky above ESO's La Silla Observatory. La Silla stands 2400 meters high in the southern Atacama Desert, with Santiago de Chile lying 600 km to the south, and it was ESO's original observing site.

ESO runs two major telescopes there, the ESO 3.6-meter telescope and the 3.58-meter New Technology Telescope (NTT). Their state-of-the-art instruments are built either entirely by ESO or by outside groups of institutions with substantial help from ESO.

La Silla also regularly hosts visiting instruments. These are attached to a telescope for a single observing run and then removed, so that the site's telescopes can take on different equipment from one observing run to the next. The observatory is also home to many national telescopes, such as the Danish 1.54-meter telescope and Switzerland's 1.2-meter Leonhard Euler Telescope.

understand.summary: This is a landscape photograph taken with a camera at an ESO site, in visible light. The camera settings and color processing are not published.
understand.eye: A long camera exposure gathers more light than the eye can, so faint stars appear more numerous here than they would to someone on the mountain.
